newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares maintain rally to end on highs.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares maintain rally to end on highs.

text.p: New Zealand shares kept up their excellent New Year form with another late rally on Tuesday, with forestry group Carter Holt Harvey again leading the way.
The NZSE-40 capital index gained 11 points to close at 2,408.28, with Carter Holt up 10 cents to $3.40.
Miles Donaldson at Hendry Hay McIntosh said the market was looking strong after the index cleanly broke key resistance at 2,391 on Monday. "That was a very bullish sign for us," he said.

Interest out of Asia and Australia contributed to the strong close and ramped up the Carters price, in particular. Donaldson said sentiment towards forestry stocks globally had improved, with the Standard and Poor's paper and forest index rising 1.01 percent overnight.

Fletcher Building continued its fine run, adding eight cents to $4.62 after touching a low of $4.50. Scrip was tight, with only 270,000 shares traded. Donaldson said construction stocks were strongly in favour in view of increased government spending under the centre-right coalition unveiled last month.
Elsewhere, Telecom gained two cents to $7.41 and Air New Zealand "A" shares firmed seven to $2.80.
